turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen's mother, Meredith Kalinowski, sits down across from you. "Right. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so I'd like to start with the zero. Who gave it to him, and when?"
Meredith: "Don't thank me yet. Owen found out his mark from his phone, in the middle of your class. Nobody called me first. Explain that."
Owen is a great kid. Really bright, one of my favourites.
"Then you'll understand why I don't want to hear it from a gradebook. Owen is my son, and I'm not here to talk about his character. What's your evidence that he didn't write this essay?"
I'm sure this is all just a misunderstanding.

"'Sure' and 'misunderstanding' are two things I can't write down. Show me the essay, the checker's report, and whatever else you have, with dates on them. Then we'll see what kind of misunderstanding it is."
So can we agree he's a good student?
"Owen's record speaks for itself, and I'm not trading it for a compliment. What I want to know is what you based this zero on, and whether you spoke to him before you entered it."
